rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors., (1987) 1 SCC 395
rules.relevance: This case established the 'Precautionary Principle' in Indian environmental law, which the NGT applied in the present case. The principle states that where there are threats of serious and irreversible damage to the environment, the lack of full scientific certainty should not be used as a reason for postponing measures to prevent environmental degradation.

rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors., (1997) 2 SCC 353
rules.relevance: This case established the 'Polluter Pays Principle' in Indian environmental law, which the NGT did not apply in the present case. The principle states that the polluter should bear the cost of remedying the environmental damage caused by their actions.

rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors., (1997) 2 SCC 353
rules.relevance: This case also established the 'Sustainable Development Principle' in Indian environmental law, which the NGT did not apply in the present case. The principle states that development should take place in a manner that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors., (1997) 2 SCC 353
rules.relevance: This case also established the 'Intergenerational Equity Principle' in Indian environmental law, which the NGT did not apply in the present case. The principle states that the present generation should ensure that the environment is protected and preserved for the benefit of future generations.

rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors., (1997) 2 SCC 353
rules.relevance: This case also established the 'Intra-generational Equity Principle' in Indian environmental law, which the NGT did not apply in the present case. The principle states that the present generation should ensure that the environment is protected and preserved for the benefit of all sections of society, including the poor and marginalized.

rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India & Ors., (1997) 2 SCC 353
rules.relevance: This case also established the 'Public Trust Doctrine' in Indian environmental law, which the NGT did not apply in the present case. The doctrine states that natural resources are held in trust by the government for the benefit of the public and that the government has a duty to protect and preserve these resources for the benefit of the public.
